sources.citation: Meinhof, Carl. 1889-90. Das Verbum in der Isubu-Sprache: Versuch einer grammatischen Darstellung. Zeitschrift fuer afrikanische Sprachen 3: 206-234.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: WID Offsite Storage Philol 889
sources.note: Par. 3 'Lautlehre' (p. 208) is based solely on Merrick's orthography: vowels, consonant correspondences with Duala/Benga; no accent rule (only 'Dass unbetontes u und o vor Vokalen zu w, i zu y werden, versteht sich von selbst'). Par. 33 (p. 223) quotes Merrick's dictionary: 'there is always a tone accent on the word ma, to distinguish the perfect tense from the past' -- a grammatical tone/accent remark, not a word-stress rule.

sources.citation: Saker, Alfred J.S. (ed., from Joseph Merrick's incomplete MS). 1852. A grammar of the Isubu tongue. Baptist Mission Press. 41 numbered pp. + tables. Google Books W8ANAAAAQAAJ (Bodleian copy), full view.
sources.note: Orthography (pp. 1-3) gives letter values, long/short vowels, vowel coalescence and euphonic changes only; no statement on word accent or tone anywhere in the 41 pages (grammar breaks off in the verb chapter). Only prosodic remark is p. 19: for emphasis 'the Isubus prolong the word' (nden-den-dene 'great').
